publication.authors: Berg L.J., Franzen J., Buness A. et al.
publication.title: Protracted Fate Acquisition and Epigenetic De-Aging During Induced Neural Stem Cell Conversion of Human Blood Cells

public_reuse.reuse_scope: Author-published non-identifying group-level RNA differential-expression counts from the open-access article. Reuse under CC BY 4.0 with full attribution; no dbGaP expression values downloaded.
public_reuse.restriction: License of publication does not override controlled access to human individual-level sequence or expression records.

derived_published_summary.biological_context: The article states RNA-seq transcriptomic differences in cell identity continue from D14 to LP and later, and donor-age-related differential expression diminishes; this does not prove independence of chronological ageing and differentiation or establish a causal mechanism.
derived_published_summary.source_methods: Bulk QuantSeq 3'-mRNA-seq, STAR/GRCh38 alignment, featureCounts, limma with donor block via duplicateCorrelation, sex/batch covariates, BH-FDR correction.
derived_published_summary.threshold: FDR < 0.05 with study-specific filtering and comparisons
derived_published_summary.age_group_limitation: Young donor group n=3, old/intermediate age classes span decades; group-level DEGs are not donor-specific.

citation: Berg LJ, Franzen J, Buness A, et al. Protracted Fate Acquisition and Epigenetic De-Aging During Induced Neural Stem Cell Conversion of Human Blood Cells. Aging Cell. 2026;25(10):e70751. doi:10.1111/acel.70751. Figure 3D,E. Licensed CC BY 4.0.
